At each achieved state, the **pointwise ZTCF (drift)** and **pointwise ZVCF
(control)** accelerations decompose the model response under the original MATLAB
convention: drift carries velocity terms and gravity once; control applies
declared torques with velocities zeroed and gravity off in the ZVCF operand.

With $M(z)\dot v+h(z,v)=\bar B u$ and applied generalized load
$\tau_{\mathrm{ID}}=\bar B u$,

$$
a_{\mathrm{ZTCF}}=-M(z)^{-1}h(z,v),\qquad
a_{\mathrm{ZVCF}}=M(z)^{-1}\tau_{\mathrm{ID}},
$$ {#eq-zvcf_accel}

evaluated under the ZVCF protocol on the control side. At the same state,

$$
\dot v=a_{\mathrm{ZTCF}}+a_{\mathrm{ZVCF}}.
$$ {#eq-zvcf_id}

Integrated counterfactual trajectories do not inherit this sum.

The **zero-velocity baseline load** $h_0(z)=h(z,0)$ and acceleration
$-M(z)^{-1}h_0(z)$ answer a different question (configuration-dependent bias
at zero velocity). Label that diagnostic explicitly; it is not the ZVCF control
component.

At the same configuration, the velocity-dependent drift increment is

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{vel.\,drift}}:=-[h(z,v)-h(z,0)],\qquad
\tau_{\text{drift}}=-h(z,0)+\tau_{\mathrm{vel.\,drift}}=-h(z,v).
$$ {#eq-zvcf_split}

This difference contains every retained term that changes under the specified
velocity reset, including viscous damping. It is not generally a purely
inertial term. Velocity reset does not remove stiffness, stored elastic energy,
activation, or history encoded in retained internal states.

**Force evaluation does not identify stiffness.** Tangent stiffness is a
derivative of force with respect to displacement under stated loading and
boundary conditions. Material elasticity and geometric stiffness from
prestress can both contribute at zero velocity. For a beam under constant
tension $N>0$, the transverse restoring operator contains
$EI\,w_{ssss}-N\,w_{ss}$ even when $w_t=0$. Centrifugal loading is one possible
source of prestress; it is not the definition of geometric stiffness.
Zero-velocity baseline subtraction is one reproducible way to partition loads.
Direct evaluation of the declared equation terms is another. Neither establishes
material and geometric stiffness separately without the tangent model.

The useful golf question is therefore precise: how much does a specified load
change when velocity is reset, and how sensitive is the answer to retained
shaft deformation, grip conditions, and contact? This exposes interactions
without calling a hypothetical frozen state a physically passive golfer.
